newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamists accuse state of discrimination.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamists accuse state of discrimination.

text.p: An Islamist human rights association on Friday accused the Turkish state of discrimination for enforcing a strictly secularist dress code that bans Islamic clothing.

"Currently, the representatives of some state institutions are spreading enmity among people through separatist acts that discriminate against people according to their dress," said Sadi Carsancakli, chairman of the Istanbul office of Mazlum-Der.
The military-dominated National Security Council (MGK) has demanded that Turkey's first Islamist-led government implement measures aimed at cracking down on rising Islamist activism.
One demand was for full implementation of the secularist dress code, introduced by the founder of the Turkish republic, Kemal Ataturk, but rarely enforced in recent years.
"Police have detained over 30 people that we know of, and 90 that we have heard of, for their Islamic headgear and clothing. This is ridiculous, unacceptable," Carsancakli said.
Carsancakli, a lawyer, said the arrests were contrary to Article 312 of the penal code under which it is a crime to promote differences among people based on race, religion or class.

"The MGK decisions are against human rights and the freedom of dressing in accordance with your thoughts or beliefs. It is not for the state or the military to decide on how people are dressed," he added.
